title: Chapter 137 — Situational Scenarios
intro: Real-world practice for the moments that test you.

sections.title: The Online Price Comparison
sections.content: Customer shows you their phone with a lower price from Amazon. Wrong response: 'We cannot match online-only retailers.' Right response: look at their phone, acknowledge the price, then walk through the comparison stack — delivery, installation, haul-away, local service, warranty administration, no shipping damage risk. Then: 'I can match that price and you still get everything I just described. Let me write it up.'

sections.title: The Three-Month Wait
sections.content: Customer has been waiting three months for a backordered part. They are beyond frustrated. Wrong response: 'The manufacturer has not shipped it yet.' Right response: 'I understand how unacceptable this wait is. Let me escalate this directly with the manufacturer today. I am going to get a name and a commitment. You will hear from me by end of day regardless. And let me check whether we have alternative solutions — a replacement unit, a loaner, or an equivalent that is available now.'

sections.title: The Competitor's Customer
sections.content: Customer bought from a competitor but wants you to service it. Wrong response: 'You should go back to where you bought it.' Right response: 'I am happy to help. Let me see what we can do for you.' Help them. Solve their problem. Earn their next purchase. The customer who comes to you because their seller failed is the easiest acquisition you will ever make.

sections.title: The 'I Know Someone' Customer
sections.content: Customer implies they know the owner or a manager and expects special treatment. Stay professional. 'That is great — [owner name] is wonderful. Let me make sure I take great care of you.' Treat them exactly like every other customer — with excellent service. If they genuinely have a relationship with the owner, the owner will handle any special arrangements. Your job is to sell professionally.
